approachQuestion.prompt:
A spacing statistic

Given n integer positions, return the kth smallest absolute difference among all unordered pairs of distinct indices, counting equal distances separately. Input may be reordered. 2 <= n <= 200000; 0 <= positions[i] <= 10^9; 1 <= k <= n*(n-1)/2. Examples: [1,4,4], k=2 -> 3 (distances 0,3,3); [2,2], k=1 -> 0. Prefer scalable worst-case time, then memory.
constraints: Use only the stated input ordering and access guarantees.

options.text: Sort positions in place with heapsort. Binary-search distance d from 0 to max-min. For each d count pairs at distance <=d using a left pointer that only advances as the right pointer scans; retain the first d with count>=k.
options.feedback: Counting all pairs under a distance threshold gives a monotone rank predicate without materializing the quadratic pair multiset.

options.text: Sort a copied buffer with heapsort, then run the same distance search and pair counter.
options.feedback: This returns the same statistic, but copying an input that may be reordered adds avoidable storage.

options.text: Return the kth adjacent difference in sorted order, ignoring nonadjacent pairs.
options.feedback: For [1,2,4], k=3, pair distances are 1,2,3, but there are only two adjacent differences; the requested rank still exists.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For target-method, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. D=max(positions)-min(positions). Analyze in-place iterative heapsort followed by distance search with a full two-pointer count per candidate. Include sorting. Signed 64-bit counters and constant-time operations; no copies or recursion. Input storage and returned result storage are excluded; all temporary buffers and call stacks are included.
constraints: Use worst-case bounds. Count all working memory including any stack; exclude supplied inputs and the scalar result.

options.text: O(n log n + n log(D + 2)) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(n log n + n log(D + 2)) time, O(n + 1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Add sorting to a linear pair-count scan per searched distance.
details: In-place heapsort costs O(n log n). Each of O(log(D+2)) distance trials runs an O(n) two-pointer count, giving O(n log n+n log(D+2)) total. Iterative sorting and scalar counting retain O(1) auxiliary space.
“O(n log n + n log(D + 2)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Counting all pairs under a distance threshold gives a monotone rank predicate without materializing the quadratic pair multiset.
“O(n log n + n log(D + 2)) time, O(n + 1) auxiliary space”: Iterative heapsort reuses the supplied coordinate array and pair counting uses scalar indices, so no n-entry auxiliary copy is allocated.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The initial sort and each distance-feasibility scan require growing work; one constant-time query cannot replace them.
